entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cool, calculating approval — it rates a thing by the edge it hands you and says nothing about whether that edge is deserved or does any good.
examples: a contract advantageous to our country

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and firmly approving — it credits the thing with actually improving matters, where *advantageous* only counts the edge gained.
examples: an arms limitation agreement beneficial to all countries
the beneficial effects of a temperate climate

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Accusatory where its neighbours approve — it treats the partiality itself as the offence rather than as a favour worth having.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmer than *advantageous*: the advantage reads as conditions tilting your way rather than as an edge coldly reckoned up.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The British spelling of *favorable*, carrying the identical tilt-in-your-favour approval with no shift in force.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same claim as *beneficial* stripped of its formality, asserting the benefit flatly instead of arguing for it.
examples: the experience was good for her

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Brisk and informal — it books a thing on the credit side without pausing to weigh how much good is in it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Broad and unemphatic approval that places a thing on the good side without naming the advantage, where *beneficial* names it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and administrative: it records that partiality is in play and leaves untouched the question *discriminatory* settles against it.
examples: a preferential shop gives priority or advantage to union members in hiring or promoting

entries.definition: inclined to respect views and beliefs that differ from your own
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm, unhedged praise for a settled disposition, crediting respect for the differing view rather than the bare patience *tolerant* stops at.
examples: a judge who is broad-minded but even-handed

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Understated almost to neutrality — the same approval as *broad-minded* with the force stripped out of it.

entries.definition: free from provincial prejudices or attachments
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and elevated, praising a sweep wide enough that no narrow attachment survives it.

entries.definition: unwilling to accept authority or dogma (especially in religion)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise with defiance in it — the openness is a refusal of dogma, not the mild receptiveness of *open-minded*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sounds a note of magnanimity, as though the openness were generosity of spirit and not merely fairness.

entries.definition: unwilling to accept authority or dogma (especially in religion)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Bookish and clinical, naming the position where *free-thinking* cheers for it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most expansive term here, praising openness as a governing principle rather than a reaction to any particular view.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain and unpretentious, asking no more than a willingness to hear the new idea out.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The coolest praise in the set — it credits forbearance, granting a view room instead of welcoming it.

entries.definition: unwilling to accept authority or dogma (especially in religion)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Defined by what it withholds, measuring out its approval as an absence of rigidity rather than any positive warmth.

entries.definition: unwilling to accept authority or dogma (especially in religion)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The longer, stiffer twin of *undogmatic*, its extra syllable pulling it further from anything conversational.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Shifts from the inner state to the visible one, crediting a confidence you can see in the bearing where *confident* merely records it.
examples: she paints with an assured hand

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Jeering and informal - the excess is not diagnosed but mocked, a swagger the word refuses to take seriously beside the flat *overconfident*.

entries.definition: having or marked by confidence or assurance
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain baseline of the family, reporting that the assurance is there without passing any verdict on whether it is warranted.
examples: his manner is more confident these days

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The straight clinical name for the fault, marking the confidence as more than warranted and leaving the derision to *cocksure*.
examples: so overconfident and impudent as to speak to the queen

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest carrier of that same excess, an everyday word that lets the overreach register as a shrug rather than an accusation.
examples: the less he knows, the more positive he gets

entries.definition: having confidence restored; freed from anxiety
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Confidence handed back rather than held all along - the settled calm of anxiety lifted, where the rest of the family says nothing about anything having been shaken.
examples: reassured by her praise he pressed on

entries.definition: showing poise and confidence in your own worth
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns the poise inward onto one's own worth and lets it show as composure, steadier-sounding than the bare *confident*.

entries.definition: showing poise and confidence in your own worth
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest label for that same belief in one's own worth, stating it where *self-assured* leans on the outward steadiness.
examples: hardly more than a boy but firm-knit and self-confident

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Measuring and cool - it rates a resemblance as very close while stopping short of calling it the same thing.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and a little grand - closeness with good cheer inside it, heartier than the merely matey *chummy*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The doubled informal form makes the closeness emphatic and knowing where *chummy* keeps it mild.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and light - friendly association on easy terms, without the depth *intimate* claims.
examples: the bartender was chummy with the regular customers

entries.definition: held together as by social or cultural ties
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving of cohesion - the bond is what holds people together, structural where *dear* is personal.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain measure of nearness in relevance or relationship, stating the proximity without the warmth or the suspicion the rest of the set add.
examples: we are all … in close sympathy with …

entries.definition: held together as by social or cultural ties
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The open form spells the binding out and reads more deliberate and descriptive than the compact *close-knit*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Closeness figured as trust - what passes inside it is entrusted, where *chummy* is merely companionable.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling carrying the same imputation of connivance, warmth named in order to be distrusted.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Insinuating - the closeness is treated as connivance, so the snugness of the word becomes the accusation.
examples: a cozy arrangement with the police

entries.definition: with or in a close or intimate relationship
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Affectionate and avowed - the close relationship is felt as fondness, where *thick* merely reports the association.
examples: my sisters and brothers are near and dear

entries.definition: having mutual interests or affections; of established friendship
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Closeness worn as ease - an established friendship that needs no ceremony, less ardent than *intimate*.

entries.definition: with or in a close or intimate relationship
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain and understated for the same close relationship - it vouches for the bond rather than professing feeling as *dear* does.

entries.definition: having mutual interests or affections; of established friendship
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest claim in the set - mutual affection and settled friendship, closer and more private than *familiar*.
examples: pretending she is on an intimate footing with those she slanders

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunter than *approximate* for the same degree of resemblance - it asserts the likeness flatly instead of hedging it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunt informal shorthand for being closely associated, reporting the tie without the warmth *chummy* supplies.
examples: the two were thick as thieves for months

entries.definition: feeling physical discomfort or pain (‘tough’ is occasionally used colloquially for ‘bad’)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and unspecific about the body feeling wrong, naming neither the site nor the sharpness of what is felt.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: States a lack rather than a hurt — the bleakness sits in what is missing, which makes it colder than *uncomfortable*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Points at discomfort that nags and chafes, a lower-grade complaint than *painful* though the two name the same effect.
examples: bites of black flies are more than irritating: they can be very painful
